newsitem.title: ITALY: De Silguy says EMU laggards may use euro in 2002.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says EMU laggards may use euro in 2002.

text.p: EU Commissioner Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday that it could be possible for an EU nation to introduce Euro notes and coins in January 2002 even if it had failed to qualify for the launch of EMU in 1999.

"If it appears a state -- which was not included in the initial list of participants -- was able, taking into account its progress in (economic) reform, to rapidly respect the criteria, it could be possible, in my opinion, for it to introduce coins and notes at the same time as the others, that is to say on January 1, 2002," he said.
Di Silguy said that if all countries were allowed to join EMU at the planned launch date of 1999 it would be necessary to water down the strict qualifying criteria.

"We must respect the conditions laid down in the (Maastricht) Treaty," he said, adding "on the other hand, it is in everybody's interest -- for the first entrants as well as for the others -- to create a good currency from the outset."
He said it was better for a country failing to make the grade for early membership to keep up its efforts to straighten out its economy.

"It is therefore preferable for a state which does not respect the terms of reference to pursue its efforts at (economic) restructuring so as to be able in due course to benefit from a good currency, rather than immediately to join a currency of modest performance," he added.
